Definition: or ἐξώθω from G1537 and ὠθέω (to push); to expel; by implication, to propel:--drive out, thrust in.
BiblicalUsage: exōthéō is the word for drive out, thrust in. In Acts 7:45, the text says "whom God drave out before the face of our fathers."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, exōthéō means drive out, thrust in, nothing more and nothing less.
